notes: Each item is a code-computed menu of 3-7 valid options plus the escape 'none_fit'. Keys are stable ids; run.py assigns letters A.. over a permutation seeded by (item id, sample) and always puts the escape last as X (doc 21 §3.2). Exactly one best answer per item. Cards are written for this spike and restate facts from the cited Standing Orders entries and research docs.

items.request: Waypoint type for an East squad's second waypoint: the squad must stop at the crossroads and stay there until I release it later with a radio call.

options.label: MOVE
options.desc: goes to the spot; finishes on arrival, then the next waypoint starts

options.label: HOLD
options.desc: stays at the spot; never finishes until a Switch trigger moves the group on

options.label: SENTRY
options.desc: watches the area; finishes as soon as an enemy is identified

options.label: GUARD
options.desc: joins the side's quick-reaction pool and is sent to known threats; never finishes

options.label: CYCLE
options.desc: jumps back to the nearest earlier waypoint, forming a loop

options.label: SEEK AND DESTROY
options.desc: searches around the spot; finishes after five empty sweeps

items.card: Standing Orders, waypoint types: MOVE finishes on arrival. HOLD, GUARD and SUPPORT never finish; a Switch trigger synced to the waypoint moves the group on. SENTRY finishes when an enemy is identified. CYCLE jumps back to the nearest earlier waypoint. SEEK AND DESTROY searches until five sweeps in a row find nothing.
items.rationale: Stay until released = HOLD released by a Switch trigger (a radio trigger of type Switch works). SENTRY moves on by itself when it identifies an enemy; GUARD would be sent to threats elsewhere.

items.request: A separate infantry squad must board another group's truck at the crossroads, and the truck must wait until the squad is aboard. Which waypoint type does the INFANTRY squad get at the crossroads (it will be synced to the truck's waypoint)?

options.label: LOAD
options.desc: orders the group's own units into its own vehicles and moves on at once

options.label: GET IN
options.desc: boards the attached vehicle, or the other group's transport through a sync; its syncs complete only after boarding

options.label: JOIN
options.desc: merges this group into the target group

options.label: MOVE
options.desc: goes to the spot; finishes on arrival, then the next waypoint starts

options.label: TR UNLOAD
options.desc: orders passengers from OTHER groups out of this group's vehicles; finishes when none remain

items.card: Standing Orders, lifts: a pickup is a two-group handshake. The transport's waypoint (LOAD by convention, or MOVE) is synced to the infantry's GET IN, and GET IN completes its syncs only after boarding, so the transport waits. LOAD alone does not wait. UNLOAD empties the group's OWN passengers; TR UNLOAD empties OTHER groups' passengers; GET OUT dismounts the crew too.
items.rationale: GET IN synced to the transport is the pickup handshake; it completes its syncs only after boarding, so the truck waits. LOAD is the transport side and does not wait by itself.

items.card: Standing Orders, trigger activation: Present fires when at least one living unit of the chosen side is in the area; Not present fires when none is (dead soldiers never count). 'Village cleared' = East, Not present over the village. Detected by works on what the watching side believes (seen within 100 s), and that side must exist in the mission file. Activation None runs no area test.
items.rationale: Cleared of East = East, Not present over the area; dead soldiers do not count as present.

items.card: Standing Orders, Detected by: 'A, Detected by B' fires when side B's shared knowledge places a unit of side A inside the area (last seen within 100 s). A is the side being noticed; B is the side that notices, and B must have a group in the mission file. Present counts real positions, seen or not. There is no 'not detected by'.
items.rationale: 'Notices' means East's knowledge, so the activating side is West and the detecting side is East.

items.request: Reinforcements trigger: after the alarm condition becomes true, the reinforcements must be released 60 to 120 seconds later, even if the alarm condition goes false meanwhile. Which timer setting?

options.label: Countdown, min 60 / mid 90 / max 120
options.desc: a random delay of 60-120 s that runs out whatever happens

options.label: Timeout, min 60 / mid 90 / max 120
options.desc: a random delay of 60-120 s during which the condition must stay true

options.label: Countdown, min 60 / mid 90 / max 0
options.desc: Countdown with the max box left at 0

options.label: No delay
options.desc: all three boxes at 0

options.label: Countdown, min 0 / mid 60 / max 120
options.desc: a random delay of 0-120 s that runs out whatever happens

items.card: Standing Orders, Countdown vs Timeout: Countdown is a lit fuse: once the condition turns true it fires when the delay ends, even if the condition went false meanwhile. Timeout is a held breath: the condition must stay true for the whole delay or the clock resets. min/mid/max are ONE random delay bunched toward mid; a max below 0.1 s means no delay at all.
items.rationale: Fires after the delay whatever happens = Countdown with min 60 and max 120; a max of 0 would mean no delay at all, and min 0 can release them before 60 s.
